title: Speaking up: when something at work doesn't feel right

audience.assumed_prior: they know a code of conduct exists and have felt the pull to stay quiet about something
audience.why: required or encouraged training on the organisation's speak-up approach
audience.motivation: do the right thing without risking their job or relationships
audience.context: watching at a desk or on a phone between tasks, sound on, captions available

performance: When something at work does not feel right, the employee weighs it with three honest questions and raises it through a fitting channel, choosing another route when their manager is involved.

misconceptions.belief: You need proof before you speak up.
misconceptions.why_tempting: nobody wants to accuse someone wrongly, so certainty feels like the price of speaking
misconceptions.correction: Good faith means an honest belief; no proof or investigation is expected (F5).

misconceptions.belief: If your manager is involved there is nowhere to go.
misconceptions.why_tempting: the manager is the only route most people picture
misconceptions.correction: Use another channel: another manager, HR, compliance or a speak-up line (F12).

misconceptions.belief: Speaking up just gets you punished.
misconceptions.why_tempting: fear of fallout is one of the common reasons people stay silent (F2)
misconceptions.correction: Policies typically prohibit retaliation for good-faith concerns (F16).

practice_ladder.what: Maya runs the three questions on her report (s2)
Maya picks her channel with the narrator naming the options (s3)
the check twist: the viewer chooses the channel when the manager is involved

strategy.name: scenario_led
strategy.signature_move: one employee, Maya, carries the whole lesson: each section is a step she takes, and the check twists her own story
strategy.rationale: speaking up is a judgement in a social moment; a person living it makes the hesitation and the steps concrete for adults without lecturing

hook.text: Maya spots numbers on a report that do not add up, and her first thought is: say nothing.
hook.sketch: Maya at her desk, a report with one figure circled; she half-reaches for the phone, then pulls back

arc.promise: By the end you will know how to weigh a moment like this and where to take it.
arc.bridge_from_prior: Everyone has felt that pull to stay quiet; we start from it and name why it happens.

sections.title: Why we stay quiet
sections.goal: the viewer can explain the three common reasons for staying silent in terms of their own hesitation
concepts: not my business, nothing will change (F3)

sections.title: Weigh it in good faith
sections.goal: the viewer can apply three questions to decide whether a concern is worth raising, without needing proof
concepts: good faith is honest belief, not proof (F4, F5, F6)
does it break a law, policy or the code (F7)
would it be fine in public (F9)

sections.title: Pick the right channel
sections.goal: the viewer can use a fitting speak-up channel, including another route when the manager is involved
concepts: other channels: another manager, HR, compliance, speak-up line (F10)

sections.title: What happens next
sections.goal: the viewer can explain what happens after raising a concern and that retaliation is not allowed
concepts: no retaliation for good faith (F16, F17)

checks.prompt: Twist: the numbers trace back to Maya's own manager. Where does she take it now?
checks.answer: Another channel: another manager, HR, compliance or the speak-up line (F12)

arc.payoff: Back at Maya's desk: she weighs it, picks a channel, and raises it calmly; the uneasy opening moment is resolved.
arc.pocket_rule: Notice it, weigh it, take it to the right channel. You need honesty, not proof.

transfer_tasks: Find out which speak-up channels your own organisation offers.
delivery_notes: Warm and unhurried on Maya's hesitation; plain and steady on the three questions; brisk on the channels; a beat of silence on the check question.

recall_moments.prompt: The numbers trace back to Maya's own manager. Where does she take it now?
recall_moments.answer: Another channel: another manager, HR, compliance or the speak-up line (F12)

gagne.attention: the hook: Maya and the numbers that do not add up
gagne.objective: the promise right after the hook
gagne.recall_prior: s1 opens from the pull to stay quiet everyone has felt
gagne.present: s2 and s3 show the three questions and the channels on Maya's case
gagne.guidance: s2 is a worked example on Maya's report
gagne.transfer: pocket rule and the task to find your own organisation's channels

framework_audit.mayer: one character and one running example (coherence), narration over pictures not text walls (modality), names of channels shown before the check uses them (pre-training)
framework_audit.merrill: problem-centred around Maya's case; activation, demonstration, application, integration
framework_audit.arcs: relevance from a familiar hesitation; confidence from the no-proof rule and non-retaliation
